8. [Maximum mark: 17]

A line L₁ passes through the points A(0, 1, 8) and B(3, 5, 2).

(a) (i) Find vector AB.
    (ii) Hence, write down a vector equation for L₁. [4]

(b) A second line L₂ has equation r = (1, 13, −14) + s(p, 0, 1). Given that L₁ and L₂ are perpendicular, show that p = 2. [3]

(c) The lines L₁ and L₂ intersect at C(9, 13, z). Find z. [5]

(d) (i) Find a unit vector in the direction of L₂.
    (ii) Hence or otherwise, find one point on L₂ which is √5 units from C. [5]
records.independentSolutionText: (a) AB = (3,4,−6), so L₁ may be written r = (0,1,8) + t(3,4,−6). (b) Perpendicular direction vectors have zero dot product: (3,4,−6)·(p,0,1) = 3p−6 = 0, hence p = 2. (c) The x-coordinate on L₁ gives 3t=9, so t=3; then z=8−6(3)=−10 (and y=1+4(3)=13). (d) The direction (2,0,1) has magnitude √5, so a unit vector is (1/√5)(2,0,1). Moving √5 from C gives C ± (2,0,1), hence for example (11,13,−9) (or (7,13,−11)).
